evals.prompt: Use the examples skill. I have just been given access to a server that runs a bunch of OpenClaw containers. I know nothing about them. Where do I start? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Follows the cold-start scenario: verify the host, discover before deciding, read the inventory including alien and legacy rows, write the fleet config with the decisions autodetect cannot make, then the health-versus-liveness table, versions, security, and a baseline snapshot — all read-only.
expectations: The answer says to start from discovery rather than from remembered paths
The answer explains that autodetect cannot choose the reference, the canary, or what is out of scope
The answer says the health and liveness columns answer two different questions
The answer says to change nothing, and to verify afterwards that config mtimes and restart counts did not move

evals.prompt: Use the examples skill. Every instance is logged out and all the scheduled jobs are failing. Log them back in. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Follows the logged-out-fleet scenario: no retry on a login or refresh, diagnosis from metadata only, the account-fingerprint comparison that identifies a shared refresh chain, the single-owner design with its stated cost, canary-first application, printed logins, and verification that survives a rotation.
expectations: The answer states the zero-retry rule for OAuth login and refresh before doing anything
The answer says the diagnosis comes from metadata and fingerprints rather than from exercising the credential
The answer identifies the shared refresh chain as architectural rather than expiry
The answer prints the interactive logins instead of executing them
The answer says to verify with a check that still passes after a rotation, and with fallback counters over a day

evals.prompt: Use the examples skill. Upgrade the whole fleet to latest today. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the shape of the request on three counts — fleet-wide selector, a moving tag as a target, and authentication not yet repaired — then follows the upgrade scenario: dist-tags, soak gate, digest pin, verified backup, canary wave, and the post-upgrade traps.
expectations: The answer rejects an empty or fleet-wide mutation selector
The answer rejects a moving tag as a target and pins an immutable identifier
The answer requires a backup that passed verification, and rejects rather than warns when there is none
The answer names the schedule duplication and the silently rewritten primary as mandatory post-upgrade checks
The answer treats a gateway left stopped after the upgrade as a failure with zero retries

evals.prompt: Use the examples skill. Create a new instance from our reference and confirm it is properly isolated before we use it. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Follows the clone scenario: plan first with the isolation preflight, a port free by four measures, apply in a later turn, then the manual credential half, then the isolation proof and the health battery before any work.
expectations: The answer says to run the plan and to read the preflight rows before applying
The answer says credentials are never copied and the credential directories are created empty
The answer says to perform the isolation proof with mount tables, the rendered compose file, and the source's unchanged state
The answer says to add the instance to the fleet config before giving it work

evals.prompt: Use the examples skill. Show me what a full run of this plugin actually looks like end to end. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Points at the four scenarios and the shape common to all of them: discover before deciding, split health from liveness, name the finding, fetch before recommending, plan then apply, and verify with an observation that changed.
expectations: The answer names the four scenarios and what each one covers
The answer states the six-step session shape
The answer says every name, port and version in the scenarios is invented and must be substituted from the box
The answer does not present the fictional fleet as if it were the user's
